rows.citation: Clark, A. G. (2023). Establishing the Causal Foundations of Metamorphic Testing: A Novel Application of Causal Inference for Testing Computational Modelling Software. PhD thesis, University of Sheffield (White Rose eTheses Online).
rows.model_type: General computational modelling software: epidemiological equation- and agent-based models (Covasim) plus the Luo-Rudy 1991 cardiac action-potential ODE model
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - adds AddCause/DeleteCause mutation operators (CosmicRay fork) to synthetic programs; the LR91 cardiac model itself is not mutated.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - LR91 inputs sampled by Latin hypercube over six conductances; these are parameter changes, not a battery of current-clamp protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - LR91 case study uses one action-potential feature, APD90, as the tested output; no eFEL-style multi-feature vector.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - metamorphic relations come from causal graphs; no selection of a compact test or stimulus set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - case studies and synthetic controlled experiments; no discovery/held-out split of models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated edits or translations evaluated.
rows.software: Causal Testing Framework, https://github.com/CITCOM-project/CausalTestingFramework (MIT per GitHub API); LR91 example code cited at https://github.com/AndrewC19/LR91
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Tests expected cause-effect relations via causal inference; NeuroSem instead compares original vs edited neuron models across stimulus protocols, with refinement-calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: White Rose eTheses landing page (eprints/DC meta tags: title, creator, date 2023-09, institution, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); full thesis PDF read (abstract, contents, Ch.5-6 LR91 case study); GitHub REST API for CausalTestingFramework repo.
rows.found_via: Google Scholar '"metamorphic testing" neuron simulation'; thesis landing page

rows.citation: Clark, A. G., Foster, M., Walkinshaw, N., et al. (2023). Metamorphic Testing with Causal Graphs. 2023 IEEE Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST), pp. 153-164.
rows.model_type: General software: randomly generated synthetic Python programs from causal graphs, plus two Defects4J Java bugs
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - AddCause and DeleteCause operators inject causal-structure faults; mutation score measures detection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - randomly generated test suites of varying size exercise metamorphic relations; not physiological stimulus protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - program outputs only; no neuroscience or electrophysiology content.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - compares random test-suite sizes but does not optimise or greedily select tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - controlled experiments over seeded random graphs and two case studies; no held-out split.
rows.software: Experiment code cited in paper: https://github.com/AndrewC19/causal_metamorphic_relation_generation and https://github.com/AndrewC19/DAG-MT-case-studies (not checked via GitHub API)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic metamorphic-relation generation from causal graphs; NeuroSem is neuron-model-specific differential testing with electrophysiology features, calibrated tolerances, compact protocol selection and held-out generalisation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works (title, authors, venue, April 2023, pp. 153-164); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar abstract; green OA author PDF (eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/195317) read for experimental setup.
rows.found_via: Crossref title query from Clark thesis search; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works

rows.citation: Cañizares, P. C., Núñez, A., Merayo, M. G. (2018). Mutomvo: Mutation testing framework for simulated cloud and HPC environments. Journal of Systems and Software, 143, 187-207.
rows.model_type: Distributed applications (client/server, intensive computation, scientific pipeline) executed on simulated cloud/HPC platforms
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - mutated application models are generated and test suites run against them to measure effectiveness (per abstract).
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract mentions test suites of manually designed cases; full text is closed access and was not read.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - abstract describes assessing test-suite effectiveness, not selecting an optimal compact suite; methods not read.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - abstract reports a case study over three applications; no held-out design mentioned.
rows.software: MuTomVo (tool named in abstract; no URL retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Mutation analysis of test suites for simulated distributed systems; NeuroSem targets neuron models with biophysical and numerical mutation families, electrophysiology features, refinement-based tolerances and held-out protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works (title, authors, JSS vol 143, pp. 187-207, Sept 2018); Semantic Scholar Graph API abstract (closed access, abstract only; OpenAlex had no abstract).
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'mutation analysis testing scientific simulation software effectiveness of test suites'; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works

rows.citation: Valle, P., Ali, S., Arrieta, A. (2026). Exploring the Potential of Large Language Models in Simulink-Stateflow Mutant Generation. arXiv:2602.04066; also in Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM Third International Conference on AI Foundation Models and Software Engineering (FORGE), pp. 99-109.
rows.model_type: Simulink-Stateflow cyber-physical controller models (Door, Fridge, Elevator, Pacemaker)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - LLMs and a rule-based baseline generate state/transition mutants; generability, compilability, duplicate and equivalent rates measured.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - engineer-written suites of 10-16 coverage-driven test cases per model; a mutant is detected if any test output differs.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares controller output signals; no feature extraction or electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - test suites are fixed; the study optimises prompting/temperature for mutant generation, not test selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - four case-study models evaluated; no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - LLMs produce the mutants; potentially equivalent mutants are sampled and manually checked, but AI edits are not audited as repairs/refactors.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Focuses on LLM mutant generation quality for Stateflow; NeuroSem uses recorded single-fault operators on neuron models, calibrated feature tolerances, and selects stimulus protocols evaluated on held-out models and families.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page meta tags (authors, 2026-02-03, abstract); DataCite api.datacite.org for arXiv DOI; arXiv PDF read (case studies, test suites, equivalence method); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/3793655.3793737 for the FORGE version (DOI printed in PDF); GitHub REST API for repo/license.
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'mutation analysis SBML systems biology model test suite fault injection'; arXiv abstract page

rows.citation: Waltemath, D., Henkel, R., Hälke, R., et al. (2013). Improving the reuse of computational models through version control. Bioinformatics, 29, 742-748.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - identifies and explains differences between existing model versions; no fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - structural XML comparison; no simulation under stimuli described in the abstract.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no simulation outputs or electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - not applicable to a version-diff approach.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - conceptual requirements plus software implementation; no evaluation split described.
rows.software: BiVeS (Biochemical Model Version Control System), http://sems.uni-rostock.de/bives/ (URL as given in abstract; not fetched)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Detects and explains structural differences between model versions; NeuroSem asks whether edits change simulated behaviour, which structural diffs alone cannot establish, via multi-protocol feature testing.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works (title, five authors, Bioinformatics vol 29, pp. 742-748, 2013, abstract); Europe PMC REST search (PMID 23335018, not open access; full text not read).
rows.found_via: Google Scholar '"functional curation" electrophysiology models protocols'; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works | Europe PMC citations of ModelDB 2004

rows.citation: Ranasinghe, N. R., Jones, S. M., Kucer, M., et al. (2025). LLM-Assisted Translation of Legacy FORTRAN Codes to C++: A Cross-Platform Study. Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on AI and Scientific Discovery: Directions and Opportunities, pp. 58-69.
rows.model_type: General scientific/HPC programs (Rosetta Code and DataRaceBench Fortran/C++ pairs)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - evaluates LLM translations; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - each program run once and its printed output compared; no input or stimulus battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - outputs tokenised, numbers rounded to 4 decimals, Jaro-Winkler similarity; no domain features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test or input selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - benchmark evaluation across LLMs and two serving platforms; no held-out design.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - open-weight LLMs translate Fortran to C++; assessed by CodeBLEU, compilation and output similarity.
rows.software: none (paper states the workflow is not yet packaged as a standalone tool)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks AI translations by one-run output string similarity; NeuroSem would test neuron-model edits across many stimuli with calibrated feature tolerances and known single-fault mutants.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works (title, eight authors, AISD 2025, pp. 58-69); ACL Anthology landing page abstract; ACL Anthology PDF read (datasets, output-similarity method, limitations); OpenAlex record.
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'LLM code translation scientific computing Fortran C++ behavioral equivalence testing' + Crossref title query; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works | DataCite (arXiv DOIs) LLM + Fortran translation; abstract via DataCite
